title.orig: 1587, a Year of No Significance: The Ming Dynasty in Decline

year_display.zh: 1981 年英文版；1982 年中文版

review.en: Huang takes an unremarkable year of the Ming and builds the book around six people: the Wanli emperor, two grand secretaries, an upright official, a general and a dissenting philosopher. Through them he argues that the empire was run on moral rhetoric rather than workable institutions and finance. The thesis is broad and sometimes too neat, but the method of seeing structure through lives is original, and its readership in Chinese has been enormous.
review.zh: 黄仁宇选取明朝平淡无奇的一年，以六个人物撑起全书：万历皇帝、两位首辅、一位清官、一位将领和一位异端思想家。借他们，他论证帝国靠道德说辞而非可行的制度和财政来运转。论点宏阔，有时过于整齐，但借人物看结构的写法很有新意，中文读者极多。
